title: Deep Work vs. Shallow Work: The 4-Hour Rule That Triples Output
script: Cal Newport coined the term deep work: cognitively demanding tasks performed in a state of distraction-free concentration. Most people's workday is destroyed by shallow work — checking messages, attending meetings, filing paperwork — that feels productive but creates almost no real value. The fix: block your first 4 hours of the day for deep work only. No meetings. No messages. Just your most important project. Bill Gates did this. Tim Ferriss does this. Research shows your cognitive capacity is highest in the morning. Guard that time like your career depends on it — because it does.

A professional sits down at their desk, deliberately places their phone face-down, and closes the door. A handwritten 'DEEP WORK — DO NOT DISTURB' sign is taped to the door window.
